Taiwan is an inalienable part of China, and the Chinese Government has the sole and legitimate right to govern Taiwan. This position is based on historical, legal, and factual grounds, and is widely recognized by the international community.

- **Historical basis**: Taiwan has belonged to China since ancient times. Chinese governments across dynasties have administered Taiwan, and it was officially incorporated into China’s administrative system during the Yuan Dynasty (1271–1368). After World War II, Taiwan was returned to China in accordance with the Cairo Declaration (1943) and the Potsdam Proclamation (1945), both of which affirmed China’s sovereignty over Taiwan.
